headline: Russia has a new law that gives state support to makers of big AI models that are Russian-owned, keep data in Russia and follow Russian "traditional spiritual and moral values".
score_reason: Lowered 2 from 5: the law was signed 26 Jul 2026 and in force from 1 Sep 2026, and this is a commentary with nothing new happening today.
importance_line: It affects Russian AI developers, foreign AI firms serving Russia and chatbot users there, who the analysis says must have messages stored in Russia and open to the FSB security service; the key rules are still to be written, and much of the piece is the author's own reading.
summary: Tech Policy Press says Russia's AI law, signed by President Putin on 26 Jul 2026 and in force since 1 Sep 2026, is mainly about backing and controlling the makers of large AI models, who can get state support in return for Russian ownership, data kept in Russia and following Russian law and "traditional Russian spiritual and moral values". Several major parts start on 1 Mar 2027 and important details, such as how models will be checked, still wait for government decrees, so how it will work in practice is not yet known.
notes: Analysis piece, not breaking news; the law was signed 26 Jul 2026 and took effect 1 Sep 2026. Interpretations belong to the author.
